components.name: Block Lamp
components.description: 11px state indicator: unlit socket, amber (awaiting), white (held), green (in flight), closed (rejected, extinguished).
components.css: .ds-lamp{display:inline-block;width:11px;height:11px;border-radius:50%;background:#0A100D;box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.6) inset}.ds-lamp.ds-lit-amber{background:#FFB000;box-shadow:0 0 2px rgba(255,176,0,.35),0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,.4) inset}.ds-lamp.ds-lit-green{background:#46C978;box-shadow:0 0 2px rgba(70,201,120,.3),0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,.4) inset}.ds-lamp.ds-lit-white{background:#F2F7F0;box-shadow:0 0 2px rgba(242,247,240,.3),0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,.4) inset}.ds-lamp.ds-closed{background:#050807;position:relative}.ds-lamp.ds-closed::after{content:'';position:absolute;inset:3px;border-radius:50%;border:1px solid #84998B;opacity:.5}

narrative.overview: The hub is a CTC railroad dispatcher's panel, not a job board. Every listing is a block on the line; every apply-status is a lamp the dispatcher throws. The world refuses the white-card job-board scaffold entirely: no cards, no light surfaces, no brand gradients. The material is backlit enamel — deep green-black grounds machined into panels, legends etched in near-white, indicator lamps that emit real light. One faint top-center backlight on the deck is the single ambient light source; every other glow comes from a lit lamp. Density is the point: 42px rows, 9-11px tracked caps, tabular mono figures. Committed states are hard figure-ground inversions, never tints; rejected blocks go dark the way a closed block loses its light.
keyCharacteristics: Backlit-enamel dark world: four enamel grounds, three etch inks, one groove + one ridge seam pair
Lamp semantics carry all state color; each hue has exactly one meaning
Two voices: National Park for every word, Chivo Mono for every figure
Depth by machined seams and inset shadows, not drop shadows
One authored motion moment (the repack); everything else is sub-250ms functional transition
Browser chrome is themed in-world: selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring, tabular numerals
Microcopy stays in the dispatcher's voice ("BLOCKS ON THE LINE", "SIGNAL FAILURE")

rules.name: The One Lamp, One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Amber = awaiting your decision (new and untouched). White = held (saved). Green = in flight (applied / interviewing / offer). Red = live deadline pressure only. A rejected block gets no hue at all — it goes dark (opacity .45, extinguished lamp). No signal hue may take a second job.

rules.name: The Amber Chrome Rule
rules.body: Amber is additionally the only interaction accent — focus ring, caret, selection, hover accents. Green, white-lamp, and red never appear in interaction chrome; they exist only as state.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: National Park speaks every word; Chivo Mono renders every figure, code, date, count, and key-cap (plus the scan query). No text may use a third family, and numeric columns are always tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Tracked Caps Rule
rules.body: Every label is uppercase, 9-11px, letter-spaced 0.14-0.2em, in an etch ink. Sentence-case is reserved for row titles, notes, and empty-state subtext.

rules.name: The One Moment Rule
rules.body: New motion may tune the repack; it may not add a second authored moment. Functional transitions stay at or under 0.25s.

rules.name: The Groove-and-Ridge Rule
rules.body: Every structural edge is a seam: a groove line (#0A100D) on the recessed side, a one-pixel ridge highlight (#2C3D33) inset on the raised side. New panels must be seamed, not shadowed.

rules.name: The Light-Is-Signal Rule
rules.body: Outward glow belongs exclusively to lit lamps and the thrown pip; the only drop shadow is the plate's. Decorative glows, glassy blurs, and hover drop shadows do not exist in this world.

rules.name: The Hard Inversion Rule
rules.body: A committed state is a full figure-ground flip — dark ground gains light fill and dark text (throw.on, new-ind.on, ::selection). Never a tinted or half-toned selected state.

dos: Do keep every hue on its one job: amber = awaiting decision + interaction chrome, white = held, green = in flight, red = live deadline (< 14 days, unexpired) only.
Do seam new panels with the groove (#0A100D) + ridge (#2C3D33) pair and the four enamel steps; depth is machined, never floated.
Do set every number in Chivo Mono with tabular-nums, and every label as tracked uppercase (0.14-0.2em) in an etch ink.
Do make committed states hard inversions (light ground, dark text) with aria-pressed / aria-current kept truthful.
Do theme browser chrome in-world on any new surface: amber selection and caret, enamel scrollbar, the 2px amber :focus-visible ring.
Do write microcopy in the dispatcher's voice — blocks, levers, sheets, lines, signal failure — in tracked caps for legends.
Do wrap any future motion in prefers-reduced-motion and keep functional transitions at or under 0.25s.
donts: Don't introduce white cards, light-mode surfaces, brand gradients, or imagery — the world is backlit enamel, and the deck's single radial backlight is the only ambient light.
Don't color a rejected or expired thing red — closed states lose light (dark lamp, reduced opacity, etch-faint ink), they never gain a hue.
Don't add outward glows or drop shadows beyond the plate drop and lamp/pip glows.
Don't add a third typeface, a radius beyond 5px (lamps excepted), or a non-1px border.
Don't author a second motion moment; the repack owns arrival.
Don't let render-side lamp() and client-side lampClass() drift apart when adding states — they are the same rule in two runtimes.
